newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close higher on plastics surge.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close higher on plastics surge.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished up but off a morning high on Monday as a bank's projection of soaring profits for giant Formosa Plastics group fuelled wider buying, brokers said.
The weighted index ended 63.62 points or 0.96 percent higher at 6,659.72, back from an intraday high of 6,692.89. Turnover was a modest T$59.68 billion.
Plastics and chemical shares led the surge with a 2.37 percent rise, followed by textiles' 2.12 percent gain.
A Mitsubishi Bank report said Formosa Plastics group's multibillion-dollar petrochemical project, to open in 1999, would boost the conglomerate into one of the island's best long-term investments.

The study predicted that profits for the group's three key members -- Formosa Plastics, Nan Ya Plastics and Formosa Chemical and Fiber -- would soar in 2000 after completion of the US$9 billion project. All three closed sharply higher on active buying.
"The (Formosa Plastics) report is the main reason for the rise," said Chen Han-chung, an analyst of Yungli Securities.
"But I don't think the market will rise too much or too fast because of the report. Lots of things can happen between now the the year 2000," Chen added.
The session's most-active issue, group member Formosa Chemical and Fiber, surged T$2.4 or 6.74 percent to T$38.
Lower-priced textiles also drew bargain-hunting, with Hualon Corp up 40 cents or 1.69 percent to T$24.
Electronics firm Mitac International Corp gained T$1.8 or 6.69 percent to T$28.7 in active trade.
